_comment: This is the config the ADLC uses on itself, and it doubles as the worked example: the full specialist roster, an area routing map that is machine-enforced, and one scheduled lane per stage. Concurrency here is N scheduled lanes rather than a thread pool, and every lane firing writes a ledger tick — so a lane that quietly stops shows as STALE instead of looking like a lane with nothing to report.

checks._comment: gofmt -l exits 0 whether or not it printed anything, so its OUTPUT is the verdict. Reading its exit code reads a channel that carries no information.
go_test_json counts the tests that reported a result. Zero is a FAILURE: a filter matching nothing converts 'I ran nothing' into 'everything passed'.

workers.description: Turns an intent into a written approach: what exists, what the options are, which one and why. Creates no work items.
Decomposes an approach into work items with checkable acceptance criteria. Writes no code.

workers._comment: The generalist implementer. It declares no areas, so it takes anything a specialist does not claim — which is what keeps an item in an unclaimed area from being handed to whichever specialist happens to sort first.
workers.description: Implements work items in the core of the system.
Implements the command-line surface and its output.
Implements documentation items: the README, the user docs, the prompts' own prose.

workers._comment: The engineering disciplines. Each one earns a dedicated prompt because it is prone to a different mistake — not because it touches different files. cli-dev and docs-writer above share implementer.md precisely because for them the difference IS only which files they touch.
workers.description: Interface work. The trap is building the one state you had data for, and retrofitting accessibility after the layout.
Service work. The trap is code that is correct in one process and wrong in two.
Interface contracts. The only implement work whose damage a revert cannot reach, because client code is already written against it.

workers._comment: Split from `query` on irreversibility: a migration runs once against data already there and is not undone by reverting the commit.
workers.description: Schema and migrations. Owes a rehearsal at realistic size, a lock duration, and a written rollback.
Access paths. Owes a plan and a row count at production volume, not an argument from reading the code.
Infrastructure as code and the alerting on it. The trap is alerting on causes rather than symptoms, and drift an apply silently reverts.

workers._comment: A validator rather than a builder: it reviews shape against the system. An implement item tagged `architecture` falls through to the generalist, because the routed owner does not hold implement.
workers.description: Reviews structure. The trap is blocking on taste, and reviewing a plan's description instead of its import list.
Executes the tests and reports what ran. A suite that matched nothing is a failure, not a pass.
Checks an item against its acceptance criteria by executing commands. Never the run that wrote the code.
Adversarial review against the project's invariants, and validation of a plan against the intent that produced it. The only role that may reject.
Validator specialising in what an attacker would do. Dispatched to items whose area says security is the risk.
Validator specialising in scale and load. A finding here needs a number.
Validator specialising in what is left behind when something is killed halfway.
Hygiene only: stale docs, dead references, duplicated statements of one fact. Runs rarely and changes little.
Judges a change against the system rather than against the item. The only role that looks wider than one unit of work.
Reads a landed item's own history, records what it taught, and raises self-improvements as their own work items.

workers._comment: The console is the only role with no place in the lifecycle: it advances nothing on its own, and everything it proposes goes through the same authority as everything else. It exists so a person can drive this tool by talking to it.
workers.description: Answers an operator in the dashboard and drafts actions from what they asked for. Advances no work item on its own.
The build environment, dependencies, CI — and the apply step, after an approval that named the plan.

_routing_comment: An area with no owner is a configuration error, not a warning: an item filed under one is unreachable, and an unreachable item looks exactly like one nobody has got round to yet.

loops._comment: Lanes are ordered by how near the finish line their work is, and staggered so two never fire on the same second and contend for the same lease. Work closest to done drains first: a fleet that builds faster than it checks piles up unverified work that looks exactly like progress. Cadences are short because a tick that finds nothing costs nothing — only a DISPATCH spends money, and max_per_tick is what bounds that. Long cadences on the entry lanes bought no safety and made a new project look broken for half an hour.
loops.name: improve

loops._comment: Planning is demand-driven as well as scheduled: a deliverable at its target asks for nothing, so this lane fires, finds no need, and records an idle tick rather than inventing work to justify its own cadence.
loops.name: plan

server._comment: Loopback only. This surface writes to the ledger and has no authentication; those two facts have to stay welded together.

console._comment: authority is propose | act | full. 'act' lets it do anything the control plane could do on its own, each through the same authority as everything else, and leaves the three gates a person owns as drafts you press. 'full' lets it press those too, which removes the only human checkpoint in the system — the record still says the agent did it. command: {{session_args}} keeps one conversation across turns, and --output-format stream-json --include-partial-messages is what makes the console show a turn as it happens rather than after it finishes. Those flags are written here rather than added by the tool, because the command is yours — an agent that simply prints what it is doing streams fine without them.

budget._comment: Empty on purpose. With no price entry a run reports UNPRICED — cost unknown, not zero — instead of printing $0.00 over real spend. Fill in from your provider's current pricing before running unattended.

lease._comment: A lease must outlive the longest run it protects, or two agents work the same item — which is the failure leases exist to prevent. So this is a multiple of dispatch.timeout_seconds and moves with it. It is also the ceiling on how long a killed process blocks its item, which is why neither number is larger than it has to be.

dispatch._comment: max_concurrent is the fleet-wide ceiling on agents running at once, and it is now enforced rather than merely declared. Each lane offers max_per_tick dispatches together; this bounds the total across every lane. Raising it raises the burn rate in direct proportion, so set budget.per_day_micros before raising it far.

mandatory_clauses: You never weaken, skip or delete a check to make a gate pass.
You never mark your own work done.
If you could not run something, say so.
